note: Christian Religious Studies round 3 (part A): Old Testament themes - sovereignty of God, covenant, leadership, providence, parental responsibility, obedience, David, decision-making, greed, supremacy of God, reforms in Judah, Nehemiah, faith and courage, Jonah, social justice, holiness and call, punishment and hope - scripture-based and application items.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Genesis 1 records that God gave man dominion over the fish, the birds and every living thing. A farmer who deliberately poisons a stream to kill all the fish for a quick harvest is
questions.A: exercising the dominion properly, since the fish were created for man to use as he pleases
questions.B: abusing that dominion, forgetting that man is a steward who is answerable to the Creator
questions.C: fulfilling the command to be fruitful and multiply by increasing his household's food supply
questions.D: acting within his rights, because dominion means unlimited control over every living creature
questions.explanation: Dominion in Genesis 1:26-28 is delegated authority under God, so man must care for creation as a steward, not destroy it.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In Isaiah 45, God calls Cyrus, a Persian king who did not know Him, 'my anointed' and uses him to release the exiles. This shows that
questions.A: God works only through leaders who belong to His covenant people
questions.B: Cyrus had secretly converted to the worship of the God of Israel before his conquest
questions.C: God's sovereignty extends even over rulers who do not acknowledge Him
questions.D: the Persian empire was more righteous than the kingdom of Judah had been
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:1-6 stresses that God raised up Cyrus 'though you do not know me', proving that He rules all nations and their kings.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Isaiah 45:9 asks, 'Does the clay say to him who fashions it, What are you making?' A church member who insists that God must explain why her business failed before she will keep serving Him is
questions.A: acting as the potter rather than the clay, exactly as Isaiah recommended
questions.B: showing the honest faith that Isaiah encouraged among the exiles in Babylon
questions.C: following the example of Cyrus, who demanded signs from God before acting
questions.D: questioning the Creator's purposes in the very way the prophet warned against
questions.explanation: The potter-and-clay image in Isaiah 45:9-12 teaches that the creature has no right to demand explanations from its Maker.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Psalm 19 says the heavens declare the glory of God, yet 'there is no speech, nor are there words'. The psalmist's point is that
questions.A: the sun and the stars should be honoured as gods because of their splendour
questions.B: creation bears silent but universal witness to the glory of its Creator
questions.C: God can be known only by scholars who study the movements of the stars
questions.D: the written law is unnecessary because nature teaches everything about God
questions.explanation: Psalm 19:1-4 teaches that the created order proclaims God's glory to all people everywhere without using words; verses 7-11 then praise the law.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In Genesis 1 God said, 'Let there be light,' and there was light. This manner of creation shows that
questions.A: creation was a long struggle between God and the powers of darkness
questions.B: God needed pre-existing light before He could create anything else
questions.C: God's word alone has the power to bring things into existence
questions.D: light was produced by the sun and the moon on the first day
questions.explanation: Creation by divine command (Genesis 1:3, 6, 9) reveals God's absolute sovereignty: He speaks and it is done, without effort or opposition.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God commanded Adam not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, 'for in the day that you eat of it you shall die'. This shows that
questions.A: God did not want man to gain knowledge of any kind in the garden
questions.B: the fruit of the tree was poisonous and God was protecting Adam's health
questions.C: man was created without any freedom to choose between good and evil
questions.D: God alone has the right to set limits for man, who is accountable to Him
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:16-17 presents God as the sovereign Lord who sets the boundaries of human freedom and holds man responsible for keeping them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Genesis 2:7 says God formed man of dust from the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life. This teaches that
questions.A: man is made of the same material as the animals and is no different from them
questions.B: human life is a gift that depends entirely on God
questions.C: the human body is evil because it was made from the dust of the ground
questions.D: man became a living being through his own effort and intelligence
questions.explanation: Man became 'a living being' only when God breathed life into him, so life belongs to God and is held in dependence on Him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Isaiah 45:7 says, 'I form light and create darkness, I make weal and create woe; I am the LORD, who do all these things.' A student who claims that God controls only pleasant events is corrected by this verse, which shows that
questions.A: there are two gods, one who sends good things and another who sends evil
questions.B: God is personally responsible for the evil deeds committed by human beings
questions.C: nothing happens outside God's control, whether prosperity or calamity
questions.D: calamity comes only from the devil while prosperity alone comes from God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:7 was addressed to Persians who believed in rival gods of light and darkness; the LORD alone rules over all events.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God's covenant with Noah differed from the one with Abraham in that it
questions.A: was conditional on the building of an altar every year at Shechem
questions.B: was sealed with the sign of circumcision on the eighth day after birth
questions.C: promised a land and a great nation to one particular family
questions.D: was made with every living creature on earth and required nothing of man
questions.explanation: Genesis 9:8-17: the Noahic covenant embraces all flesh and is an unconditional promise never again to destroy the earth by flood.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In Genesis 15 God passed between the pieces of the sacrificed animals as a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch while Abram slept. This signified that
questions.A: Abram had to walk through fire before he could receive the promise
questions.B: God alone bound Himself to fulfil the covenant promises
questions.C: the animals were unacceptable and had to be burnt up completely
questions.D: God rejected Abram's offering because he had fallen asleep
questions.explanation: In ancient covenants both parties passed between the pieces; here only God passed, showing that the promise rested on God's faithfulness alone.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When God changed Abram's name to Abraham and Sarai's to Sarah in Genesis 17, the change signified
questions.A: the transfer of the promise from Sarah to Hagar and Ishmael
questions.B: that Abram had been adopted into the royal family of Egypt
questions.C: a new identity tied to the promise of many nations and descendants
questions.D: a punishment for Abram's earlier lie about Sarai in Egypt
questions.explanation: Abraham means 'father of a multitude'; the new names marked the couple as bearers of God's promise of nations and kings.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At Sinai God said, 'If you will obey my voice and keep my covenant, you shall be my own possession among all peoples... a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' This shows that
questions.A: God had abandoned His earlier promises to Abraham and his descendants
questions.B: Israel was chosen because it was already holier than the other nations
questions.C: only the tribe of Levi was included in the covenant made at Sinai
questions.D: Israel's privileged position depended on obedience to God's voice
questions.explanation: Exodus 19:5-6 links the blessings of election to the condition 'if you will obey my voice and keep my covenant'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A new church member signs a membership pledge and within weeks breaks every promise in it. His behaviour resembles that of the Israelites who
questions.A: refused to accept the covenant until Moses had come down from the mountain
questions.B: promised at Sinai to obey all God's words and soon afterwards made a golden calf
questions.C: asked Aaron to read the book of the covenant to them a second time
questions.D: kept the covenant faithfully throughout the forty years in the wilderness
questions.explanation: In Exodus 24:3-8 the people said 'All that the LORD has spoken we will do'; in Exodus 32 they worshipped the golden calf.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A believer says she keeps God's commands not because a list hangs on the wall but because the desire to obey has been planted inside her. Her experience illustrates the covenant Jeremiah foretold, which differs from the Sinai covenant in that
questions.A: it must be renewed every seven years by a public reading of the law
questions.B: it applies only to the priests and Levites who serve in the temple
questions.C: the law is written on the heart and every member knows the LORD personally
questions.D: it replaces the commandments with the customs of the surrounding nations
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:31-34: 'I will write it upon their hearts... they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A feature common to the covenants with Noah, Abraham and Israel at Sinai is that
questions.A: each had the rainbow in the clouds as its sign
questions.B: each was sealed by the sprinkling of blood on the people
questions.C: each was made after the people had first kept the law perfectly
questions.D: God took the initiative in establishing each covenant
questions.explanation: In every case God Himself established the covenant (Genesis 9:9; 17:2; Exodus 19:3-6); the signs and terms differed.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In Genesis 17 an uncircumcised male was to be 'cut off from his people' because
questions.A: circumcision was required for good health in the desert
questions.B: he had broken God's covenant by rejecting its sign
questions.C: uncircumcised men were not allowed to fight in Abraham's army
questions.D: he would be unable to inherit any land in the country of Egypt
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:14 states that the uncircumcised male 'has broken my covenant'; the sign was an essential mark of belonging.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Deuteronomy 28 sets out blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience. This shows that the covenant at Sinai
questions.A: applied only to the generation that stood at the foot of the mountain
questions.B: guaranteed Israel's prosperity no matter how the people behaved
questions.C: made Israel's prosperity in the land dependent on faithfulness to God
questions.D: was concerned with worship alone and not with everyday conduct
questions.explanation: The blessings and curses of Deuteronomy 28 tie national welfare to covenant loyalty; the later exile is explained by these curses.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Pharaoh said he had heard that Joseph could interpret dreams, Joseph replied, 'It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh a favourable answer.' This shows the leadership quality of
questions.A: pride disguised as a false show of modesty before the king
questions.B: cleverness in avoiding blame if the interpretation should fail
questions.C: fear of Pharaoh, which made him deny that he had any gift
questions.D: humility that acknowledges God as the source of one's ability
questions.explanation: Genesis 41:16: Joseph pointed away from himself to God, a mark of humble leadership that later earned him Pharaoh's trust.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A school principal sets aside part of each term's fees to repair classrooms during the rainy season. She is applying the quality Joseph showed when he
questions.A: refused to eat at the same table with his brothers in Egypt
questions.B: advised Pharaoh to store grain during the seven years of plenty
questions.C: hid his silver cup in the sack of grain belonging to Benjamin
questions.D: interpreted the dreams of the butler and the baker in prison
questions.explanation: Genesis 41:33-36: Joseph's foresight and planning during plenty saved Egypt and the surrounding nations during the famine.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At the burning bush Moses objected, 'Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh?' and later, 'I am slow of speech.' God's response was to
questions.A: strike him dumb until the day he arrived in Egypt
questions.B: choose Joshua in his place because of his unbelief
questions.C: promise His presence and appoint Aaron as his spokesman
questions.D: send him back to Jethro to tend the flock for another forty years
questions.explanation: Exodus 3:12 ('I will be with you') and 4:14-16 (Aaron to speak for him) show God equipping a reluctant leader.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After the golden calf incident Moses prayed, 'If thou wilt forgive their sin - and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book.' This reveals
questions.A: fear that God would punish him for Aaron's failure
questions.B: a desire to be released from the burden of leadership
questions.C: anger at God for choosing such a stubborn people
questions.D: selfless intercession for the people he led
questions.explanation: Exodus 32:30-32: Moses was ready to lose his own place for the people's sake, a mark of shepherd-like leadership.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Barak insisted that Deborah accompany him to battle against Sisera. Deborah agreed but told him that
questions.A: God had rejected him and chosen Gideon instead
questions.B: the honour of the victory would go to a woman
questions.C: the battle would be postponed until the rains ended
questions.D: Sisera would escape and rule Israel for forty years
questions.explanation: Judges 4:8-9: because of Barak's hesitation, Sisera was killed by Jael, the wife of Heber, and the glory went to her.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God told Joshua, 'This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night... for then you shall make your way prosperous.' Joshua's success as a leader was therefore tied to
questions.A: his skill in negotiating treaties with the Canaanites
questions.B: the size of the army he had inherited from Moses
questions.C: constant meditation on and obedience to God's law
questions.D: the wealth the people had brought out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:7-9 makes courage and success depend on faithfulness to the law of Moses rather than on military strength.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A head prefect refuses to cheat in examinations while urging the junior students to be honest. He is following the example of Joshua when he
questions.A: made a treaty of peace with the deceitful men of Gibeon
questions.B: sent two spies secretly to view the land and the city of Jericho
questions.C: commanded the sun to stand still over Gibeon during the battle
questions.D: declared at Shechem, 'As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD'
questions.explanation: Joshua 24:15: Joshua led by personal example, committing himself and his household before asking the people to choose.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of his Cushite wife, and Miriam was struck with leprosy, Moses
questions.A: demanded that she be stoned outside the camp
questions.B: cried to the LORD to heal her
questions.C: removed Aaron from the priesthood as punishment
questions.D: left the camp and refused to lead the people any further
questions.explanation: Numbers 12:13: 'Heal her, O God, I beseech thee.' Moses' meekness and readiness to pray for those who opposed him mark true leadership.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Which quality did Joseph display when he revealed himself to his brothers and settled them in the land of Goshen?
questions.A: favouritism toward Benjamin at the expense of the other brothers
questions.B: cunning in luring them to Egypt so that he could enslave them
questions.C: forgiveness and generosity towards those who had wronged him
questions.D: reluctance to let his father Jacob know that he was still alive
questions.explanation: Genesis 45:4-15 and 47:11-12: Joseph forgave, comforted and settled his brothers in the best part of the land.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Abraham's servant prayed at the well that the girl who offered water to him and his camels would be the one chosen for Isaac; before he had finished praying, Rebekah came and did so. This shows that
questions.A: Abraham had arranged the marriage with Laban many years earlier
questions.B: Rebekah had been told in advance what the servant would ask
questions.C: the servant chose Rebekah because she was the most beautiful girl
questions.D: God guides those who seek His direction in specific decisions
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:12-27: the servant sought God's guidance in prayer and God directed him to Rebekah; he then worshipped the LORD.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Abraham named the place on Mount Moriah 'The LORD will provide' because
questions.A: God gave him water when he and Isaac were dying of thirst
questions.B: God provided a ram caught in a thicket in place of Isaac
questions.C: an angel brought bread and meat for the journey home
questions.D: God provided a wife for Isaac at that mountain
questions.explanation: Genesis 22:13-14: Abraham offered the ram instead of his son and called the place Jehovah-jireh, 'the LORD will provide'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jacob dreamt of a ladder reaching to heaven at Bethel and heard God say, 'I am with you and will keep you wherever you go,' he was
questions.A: a prisoner being taken down to Egypt by traders
questions.B: returning home as a wealthy man with two wives
questions.C: a fugitive fleeing from his brother Esau's anger
questions.D: leading the tribes of Israel into the land of Canaan
questions.explanation: Genesis 28:10-15: God's promise of protection came to Jacob when he was alone and running from Esau after deceiving Isaac.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the wilderness those who gathered much manna had nothing over and those who gathered little had no lack, but manna kept overnight bred worms. The lesson was
questions.A: that manna could be eaten only by the priests and Levites
questions.B: that the strong should gather for the weak in the camp
questions.C: that food should be stored for the future whenever possible
questions.D: daily dependence on God and obedience to His instructions
questions.explanation: Exodus 16:16-20: God supplied enough for each day and tested whether the people would trust Him and keep His commands.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A student who has paid this term's fees is already anxious about next year's fees. The story of the manna reminds him that
questions.A: God provides only for those who have first saved up for themselves
questions.B: God provides for each day and asks for trust rather than anxiety
questions.C: he should collect money from his classmates to be on the safe side
questions.D: God's provision for His people ended when Israel entered Canaan
questions.explanation: The daily manna (Exodus 16) taught Israel to rely on God one day at a time; hoarding out of anxiety was met with rot and worms.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At the Red Sea, with Pharaoh's army behind and the sea in front, Moses told the people, 'Fear not, stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD.' This shows that
questions.A: Moses intended to fight the Egyptian army with the men of Israel
questions.B: the people should have surrendered to Pharaoh peacefully
questions.C: God protects His people even when there is no human way of escape
questions.D: God expected the Israelites to swim across the sea by night
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:13-14: 'The LORD will fight for you, and you have only to be still'; the sea was divided for them to cross.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Moses told Israel that God fed them with manna 'that he might make you know that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of the LORD'. The wilderness experience was meant to
questions.A: keep the people from ever farming in the land of Canaan
questions.B: punish Israel for the sin of the golden calf at Sinai
questions.C: prove that manna was more nourishing than ordinary bread
questions.D: humble Israel and teach the people to depend on God's word
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 8:2-3: God humbled Israel and tested them so that they would learn to depend on Him and His word.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A woman who lost her job says, 'God allowed it, because the new job I found is far better.' Her attitude reflects Joseph's when he told his brothers,
questions.A: 'You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.'
questions.B: 'God sent me before you to preserve life.'
questions.C: 'By this you shall be tested: you shall not go from this place.'
questions.D: 'Go up in peace to your father, and take your brother with you.'
questions.explanation: Genesis 45:5-8 and 50:20: Joseph saw God's providence behind his brothers' evil act, turning it to the saving of many lives.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At Rephidim the place was named Massah and Meribah because
questions.A: Jethro visited Moses there and advised him to appoint judges
questions.B: the Amalekites were defeated there while Moses held up his hands
questions.C: the people tested the LORD, asking whether He was among them or not
questions.D: the Israelites received the Ten Commandments at that spot
questions.explanation: Exodus 17:7: Massah means 'testing' and Meribah 'contention'; the people quarrelled with Moses and doubted God's presence.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Eli's sons took the best of the sacrificial meat by force and lay with the women who served at the tent of meeting. Eli's response was
questions.A: to bring them before the elders of Shiloh for stoning
questions.B: to remove them immediately from the priesthood at Shiloh
questions.C: to hand them over to Samuel for judgment
questions.D: a mild verbal rebuke that he never backed with discipline
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:22-25: Eli only asked 'Why do you do such things?' and his sons ignored him; God said he honoured his sons above God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A father knows that his son steals from the neighbours but says, 'Boys will be boys,' and does nothing. He is repeating the failure of
questions.A: Jacob, who loved Joseph more than all his other sons
questions.B: Eli, who did not restrain his sons from their evil ways
questions.C: Abraham, who sent Ishmael away into the wilderness
questions.D: Jesse, who did not present David to Samuel at first
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:13: God judged Eli's house 'because his sons were blaspheming God, and he did not restrain them'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The message given to the boy Samuel at Shiloh was that
questions.A: the Philistines would be defeated and never trouble Israel again
questions.B: Samuel would become the first king of Israel in the place of Eli
questions.C: Eli's house would be punished for ever for the iniquity he knew of and did not restrain
questions.D: Eli's sons would be forgiven if they offered a sin offering
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3:11-14: God confirmed to Samuel the judgment already announced on Eli's family.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Phinehas' wife named her son Ichabod, saying, 'The glory has departed from Israel,' because
questions.A: the Philistines had carried away the tablets of the law
questions.B: Samuel had refused to succeed Eli as priest at Shiloh
questions.C: the temple in Jerusalem had been destroyed by the Babylonians
questions.D: the ark of God had been captured and her husband and Eli were dead
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 4:19-22: the capture of the ark, together with the deaths of Eli and his sons, marked the departure of God's glory.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After Amnon raped his half-sister Tamar, David 'was very angry' but took no action. The result was that
questions.A: Amnon repented and married Tamar according to the law
questions.B: Absalom nursed his hatred and murdered Amnon two years later
questions.C: Tamar was sent to live with her grandmother in Bethlehem
questions.D: Joab arrested Amnon and brought him before the elders
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:21-29: David's failure to discipline Amnon allowed Absalom's revenge and set off further tragedy in the family.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When David wept, 'O my son Absalom, would I had died instead of you,' Joab rebuked him because
questions.A: David had personally ordered that Absalom be killed
questions.B: Absalom had always been David's least favourite son
questions.C: his mourning shamed the soldiers who had risked their lives for him
questions.D: the law forbade a king to mourn for a rebel
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 19:5-7: Joab warned that David's grief for a rebel made his loyal men feel that he loved his enemies and hated his friends.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: King Asa removed Maacah, his mother, from being queen mother because
questions.A: she had married a foreigner after his father's death
questions.B: she had plotted with the king of Israel against him
questions.C: she refused to attend the Passover in Jerusalem
questions.D: she had made an abominable image for Asherah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:13: Asa cut down her image and burnt it, putting loyalty to God above family ties.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the elders asked Samuel for a king because his sons took bribes and perverted justice, God told Samuel that
questions.A: Samuel's sons would be punished with death for their crimes
questions.B: the people had rejected God as their king, not Samuel
questions.C: he should refuse the request and appoint Joel judge in his place
questions.D: a king would make Israel the most righteous nation on earth
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 8:7: 'They have not rejected you, but they have rejected me from being king over them.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The stories of Eli and Samuel together teach that
questions.A: sons should never be allowed to follow their fathers' profession
questions.B: the children of priests are always wicked because of their upbringing
questions.C: even godly leaders can fail as parents by not correcting their children
questions.D: a leader's children are not his responsibility once they are grown
questions.explanation: Both Eli (1 Samuel 2-3) and Samuel (1 Samuel 8:1-5) served God faithfully yet had sons who went astray, with serious national consequences.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At Gilgal Saul offered the burnt offering himself because Samuel delayed and the people were scattering. Samuel's verdict was that
questions.A: the Philistines would now be defeated because of his sacrifice
questions.B: he had acted wisely to keep the army together before the battle
questions.C: he should be made high priest as well as king over Israel
questions.D: his kingdom would not continue because he had not kept God's commandment
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 13:13-14: 'You have done foolishly... now your kingdom shall not continue'; God sought a man after His own heart.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Saul spared Agag and the best of the sheep and oxen, claiming that he kept them to sacrifice to the LORD. His basic fault was
questions.A: excessive generosity towards the Amalekite prisoners
questions.B: partial obedience, which God counts as rebellion
questions.C: cowardice in the face of the Amalekite army
questions.D: delay in going to war when Samuel commanded him
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:22-23: Saul obeyed in part but disregarded the command to destroy everything; Samuel called this rebellion and stubbornness.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Samuel told Saul that 'rebellion is as the sin of divination, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry' in order to show that
questions.A: the Amalekites practised divination and therefore deserved destruction
questions.B: Saul had secretly consulted a medium before the battle with Amalek
questions.C: disobedience to God is as grave as witchcraft and the worship of other gods
questions.D: Saul should offer more sacrifices to atone for his stubbornness
questions.explanation: Samuel equated Saul's disobedience with practices Saul himself had banned, showing how seriously God views disobedience.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A treasurer who alters the accounts says, 'The chairman insisted, and I was afraid of losing my job.' His excuse resembles Saul's when he said,
questions.A: 'Honour me now before the elders of my people.'
questions.B: 'I have performed the commandment of the LORD.'
questions.C: 'The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you.'
questions.D: 'I feared the people and obeyed their voice.'
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:24: Saul blamed the people's pressure for his disobedience; fear of men is not accepted as an excuse before God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After his rejection Saul begged Samuel, 'Honour me now before the elders of my people.' This shows that Saul was more concerned about
questions.A: the welfare of the elders than about his own position
questions.B: his public image than about genuine repentance
questions.C: restoring the Amalekite spoil to its rightful owners
questions.D: Samuel's safety on the journey back to Ramah
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:30: Saul's plea was for outward honour, not for restoration with God, unlike David's later repentance.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A student asked to write a ten-page project submits five pages and says, 'These are the best pages anyway.' His attitude mirrors that of
questions.A: Jonah, who fled to Tarshish instead of going to Nineveh
questions.B: Achan, who hid the devoted things under the floor of his tent
questions.C: Saul, who kept the best of the sheep and oxen against God's command
questions.D: Lot's wife, who looked back at the city of Sodom
questions.explanation: Like Saul in 1 Samuel 15, the student substitutes his own judgment of what is 'best' for full obedience to the instruction given.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After pronouncing God's rejection of Saul, Samuel
questions.A: fled to the Philistines for fear of Saul's anger
questions.B: anointed Jonathan as king in his father's place
questions.C: joined Saul in the sacrifice and blessed his reign
questions.D: grieved over Saul and did not see him again until the day of his death
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:35: Samuel did not see Saul again until his death but mourned for him; the LORD then sent him to anoint David.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and became a pillar of salt, and Achan hid the devoted things and was stoned. Together these episodes teach that
questions.A: God punishes only those who lead others into sin
questions.B: disobedience to a clear command of God brings certain judgment
questions.C: women and men are judged by different standards
questions.D: God's commands may be ignored if no one is harmed
questions.explanation: Genesis 19:26 and Joshua 7 both show that a direct command of God cannot be disregarded without consequence.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: When Samuel saw Eliab he thought, 'Surely the LORD's anointed is before him,' but God said, 'Man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.' This teaches that
questions.A: Samuel had lost the ability to hear God's voice in his old age
questions.B: the eldest son should always be preferred for leadership
questions.C: God chooses leaders by their character rather than their appearance
questions.D: physical strength is the most important quality in a king
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 16:6-7: David, the youngest and a shepherd, was chosen over his impressive brothers because of his heart.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: David told Goliath, 'You come to me with a sword and a spear, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts.' This shows that David
questions.A: wanted to impress Saul's daughter with his bravery
questions.B: had no weapon at all and expected to die in the valley
questions.C: relied on the training he had received in Saul's army
questions.D: placed his confidence in God rather than in weapons
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:45-47: David's trust was in the LORD, who 'saves not with sword and spear'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: A student prefers her own well-practised study method to an unfamiliar one that a friend insists on. Her choice is like David's when he
questions.A: took Saul's spear and water jar while he slept
questions.B: refused Saul's armour because he had not tested it
questions.C: danced before the ark with all his might
questions.D: refused to drink the water from the well of Bethlehem
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:38-40: David put off Saul's armour, saying 'I am not used to them', and went with his sling and five stones.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: When Michal despised David for dancing before the ark, David replied that he would make himself even more contemptible for the LORD's sake. This shows
questions.A: that David had drunk too much wine during the procession
questions.B: disrespect for his wife and for the dignity of a king
questions.C: wholehearted devotion to God regardless of human opinion
questions.D: that David wanted to shame the house of Saul publicly
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:20-22: David's joy before the LORD mattered more to him than his image before people.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: God's promise through Nathan that David's house and throne would be established for ever is known as
questions.A: the new covenant written on the heart of every believer
questions.B: the Sinai covenant, given through Moses to Israel
questions.C: the covenant of circumcision made with Abraham
questions.D: the Davidic covenant, fulfilled in Christ, the Son of David
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:12-16: God promised David an everlasting dynasty; the New Testament sees this fulfilled in Jesus (Luke 1:32-33).

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: A governor pays the school fees of the children of a late friend who once helped him. He is imitating David's treatment of
questions.A: Uriah the Hittite, whom he placed in the front line of battle
questions.B: Mephibosheth, Jonathan's lame son, who ate at the king's table
questions.C: Shimei, who cursed him as he fled from Absalom
questions.D: Nabal, who refused to give food to his men in the wilderness
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9: David showed kindness to Mephibosheth 'for Jonathan's sake', restoring Saul's land to him and giving him a place at table.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: David refused to accept Araunah's threshing floor and oxen as a gift, saying, 'I will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God which cost me nothing.' This teaches that
questions.A: offerings may be made only on land bought from Jebusites
questions.B: a king must never accept gifts from foreigners
questions.C: true sacrifice to God must cost the giver something
questions.D: God rejects any offering made on a threshing floor
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:24: David paid fifty shekels of silver; genuine worship involves real personal cost.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: In the wilderness of Ziph David proved to Saul that he had spared his life by showing
questions.A: the letter Jonathan had written to warn him of danger
questions.B: the piece of Saul's robe he had cut off in the cave
questions.C: the armour Saul had lent him for the fight with Goliath
questions.D: Saul's spear and the jar of water taken from beside his head
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 26:11-16: David took the spear and water jar but would not lift his hand against the LORD's anointed.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: In his prayer of repentance David said, 'Against thee, thee only, have I sinned.' This shows that he
questions.A: believed that Bathsheba and Uriah had not really been wronged
questions.B: recognised that every sin is ultimately an offence against God
questions.C: thought his sin was too small for anyone else to notice
questions.D: wanted to keep the whole matter secret from Nathan
questions.explanation: Psalm 51:4: David saw his adultery and murder chiefly as sin against God, whose law he had despised (2 Samuel 12:9).

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Solomon's decision to marry many foreign women led, in his old age, to
questions.A: the building of a second temple for the worship of the LORD
questions.B: peace with all his neighbours and a long, prosperous reign for his son
questions.C: his heart being turned after other gods and the kingdom being divided
questions.D: the conversion of the surrounding nations to the God of Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:1-13: Solomon's wives turned his heart to other gods, and God tore the kingdom from his son, leaving one tribe.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God gave Solomon riches and honour in addition to wisdom because
questions.A: he promised to build the temple within seven years
questions.B: he had offered a thousand burnt offerings at Gibeon
questions.C: he was the son of David and the grandson of Jesse
questions.D: he had not asked for long life, riches or the death of his enemies
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:11-13: God commended Solomon's unselfish request and added what he had not asked for.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A newly elected class captain listens to the older students and eases some petty rules, and the class co-operates with him. He is following the advice that
questions.A: the young men gave Rehoboam at Shechem
questions.B: the elders gave Rehoboam at Shechem
questions.C: Jeroboam gave the ten tribes at Shechem
questions.D: Ahijah the prophet gave Solomon at Shiloh
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:7: the elders told Rehoboam that if he served the people and spoke good words to them they would be his servants for ever.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The immediate consequence of Rehoboam's harsh answer at Shechem was that
questions.A: Egypt invaded Jerusalem and carried away the temple treasures
questions.B: the people of Judah stoned him and chose a new king
questions.C: ten tribes rejected the house of David and made Jeroboam king
questions.D: the elders resigned and left him without any advisers
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:16-20: 'What portion have we in David?'; Israel went to their tents and made Jeroboam king over the ten tribes.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God did not tear the kingdom from Solomon in his own lifetime because
questions.A: Solomon's wisdom outweighed his idolatry
questions.B: Solomon repented and destroyed the high places
questions.C: the people of Israel prayed for their king
questions.D: of His promise to David, Solomon's father
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:12: 'For the sake of David your father I will not do it in your days, but I will tear it out of the hand of your son.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A new manager ignores the experienced staff and follows the advice of his university friends, who tell him to tighten every rule. He is repeating the error of
questions.A: Solomon, who asked God for wisdom at Gibeon
questions.B: Rehoboam, who forsook the counsel of the elders
questions.C: Jeroboam, who set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan
questions.D: David, who numbered the people against Joab's advice
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:8: Rehoboam 'forsook the counsel which the old men gave him' and took the counsel of the young men, losing ten tribes.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: For a student choosing a career, the lesson of Solomon's request at Gibeon is that
questions.A: career choices should be left entirely to one's parents
questions.B: one should ask God for riches first and for wisdom afterwards
questions.C: an understanding heart for serving others matters more than wealth or fame
questions.D: the most profitable profession is always the will of God
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:9: Solomon asked for 'an understanding mind to govern thy people', and God was pleased with this priority.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Solomon's judgment between the two women who each claimed the living child was remarkable because
questions.A: the child was old enough to identify his own mother
questions.B: both women confessed the truth as soon as they saw the king
questions.C: the king had known both women before they came to court
questions.D: there were no witnesses and the claims could not be checked in any ordinary way
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:16-28: with no evidence, Solomon's order to divide the child exposed the true mother through her compassion.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jeroboam decided to set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan so that
questions.A: the Egyptians would recognise him as a lawful king
questions.B: the people would not go to Jerusalem to worship and return to Rehoboam
questions.C: the Levites would have more places at which to serve
questions.D: the ark of the covenant could be moved to the north
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:26-30: Jeroboam feared that pilgrimages to Jerusalem would win the people back; his decision became 'a sin' for Israel.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Naboth refused to sell his vineyard to King Ahab because
questions.A: he wanted to sell it to Jezebel's relatives instead
questions.B: the king offered a price far below its market value
questions.C: the LORD forbade him to give away the inheritance of his fathers
questions.D: the vineyard belonged to the priests of Jezreel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:3: 'The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers'; the law protected family land.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Naboth refused, Ahab went home vexed and sullen, lay on his bed, turned away his face and would eat no food. This shows that greed
questions.A: is found only among the poor who lack necessities
questions.B: is easily overcome by fasting and rest
questions.C: affected Ahab less than it affected Jezebel
questions.D: produces discontent even in a man who owns a kingdom
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:4: Ahab, who had everything, was miserable over one man's vineyard, showing the restless nature of covetousness.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: An official forges signatures and hires false witnesses in order to seize a widow's land. His methods resemble those of
questions.A: Gehazi in collecting gifts from Naaman the Syrian
questions.B: Jezebel in obtaining Naboth's vineyard for Ahab
questions.C: Achan in taking the devoted things from Jericho
questions.D: Ahab in pleading with Naboth to sell the vineyard
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:8-14: Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name and set two worthless men to accuse Naboth falsely so that he was stoned.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Ahab tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and fasted after Elijah pronounced judgment on him, God
questions.A: struck Jezebel with leprosy for the rest of her life
questions.B: cancelled the judgment and restored the vineyard to Naboth's sons
questions.C: postponed the disaster on his house to the days of his son
questions.D: sent Elijah to anoint Ahab a second time as king
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:27-29: because Ahab humbled himself, God delayed the evil on his house until his son's days.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Gehazi's greed was made worse by the fact that he
questions.A: confessed to Elisha before he was found out
questions.B: shared the gifts with the sons of the prophets
questions.C: returned the gifts to Naaman when he was confronted
questions.D: lied both to Naaman and to Elisha in order to cover it up
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:22-25: Gehazi invented a story about two visiting prophets and then told Elisha 'Your servant went nowhere'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Elisha refused Naaman's gift because he wanted Naaman to understand that
questions.A: prophets in Israel were paid only by the king
questions.B: the healing was a free gift of God, not a service bought with money
questions.C: Syrian silver was unclean and could not be used in Israel
questions.D: Naaman should give the money to the poor of Damascus instead
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:15-16: 'As the LORD lives, whom I serve, I will receive none'; God's grace cannot be purchased.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Because Achan secretly took a mantle, silver and gold from Jericho,
questions.A: Joshua was removed as leader and replaced by Caleb
questions.B: the walls of Jericho were rebuilt by the Canaanites
questions.C: Israel was defeated at Ai and about thirty-six men died
questions.D: the ark of the covenant was captured by the Philistines
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:1-5: Achan's hidden greed brought defeat and death on the whole nation before he was exposed and punished.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The punishment of Gehazi with Naaman's leprosy, which would cling to his descendants, teaches that
questions.A: servants should never handle money on behalf of their masters
questions.B: leprosy was the normal punishment for any lie told in Israel
questions.C: prophets had power to curse anyone who displeased them
questions.D: dishonest gain can bring lasting harm to the greedy person and his family
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:27: the silver Gehazi gained cost him his health, his position and his family's future.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following best describes what Ahab, Gehazi and Achan had in common?
questions.A: Each was a priest who misused the offerings of the people
questions.B: Each desired what was not his and brought judgment on himself
questions.C: Each repented immediately and was fully restored
questions.D: Each was a foreigner who did not know the law of God
questions.explanation: Ahab (1 Kings 21), Gehazi (2 Kings 5) and Achan (Joshua 7) all coveted what God had not given them and suffered for it.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Elijah told Ahab, 'There shall be neither dew nor rain these years, except by my word.' The drought was intended to show that
questions.A: the northern kingdom deserved to be destroyed by famine
questions.B: Elijah was more powerful than any prophet before him
questions.C: the LORD, not Baal the supposed god of rain, controlled the weather
questions.D: Ahab should build irrigation canals for the farmers
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:1: Baal was worshipped as the god of rain and fertility; the drought exposed his powerlessness and the LORD's supremacy.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: On Mount Carmel Elijah mocked the prophets of Baal: 'Cry aloud, for he is a god; either he is musing, or he has gone aside, or he is on a journey, or perhaps he is asleep.' He was
questions.A: admitting that the LORD was also slow to respond
questions.B: encouraging the prophets to pray with greater sincerity
questions.C: suggesting that Baal would answer later in the day
questions.D: exposing the helplessness of an idol that could not hear or answer
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:27: Elijah's sarcasm highlighted that Baal was no god at all, in contrast to the LORD who answered by fire.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Elijah had twelve jars of water poured over the sacrifice and the wood before he prayed, so that
questions.A: the wood would burn more slowly and be seen by all
questions.B: no one could claim that the fire was a trick or an accident
questions.C: the people would have water to drink after the drought
questions.D: the prophets of Baal could not steal his sacrifice
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:33-35: the drenched altar made the fire that fell an unmistakable act of God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, the dust and the water, the people
questions.A: demanded that Ahab kill Elijah at once
questions.B: ran away in fear to the brook Kishon
questions.C: fell on their faces and said, 'The LORD, he is God'
questions.D: asked the prophets of Baal to try again
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:38-40: the people confessed the LORD as God and, at Elijah's command, seized the prophets of Baal.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The widow of Zarephath said to Elijah, 'Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth,' after
questions.A: Elijah killed the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel
questions.B: her jar of meal and cruse of oil first failed to run out
questions.C: rain finally fell on the land after three years
questions.D: Elijah raised her son from the dead
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:17-24: the raising of her son convinced the Gentile widow of the LORD's power and Elijah's authority.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A trader who consults a herbalist for charms 'just in case' while also attending church is doing what Elijah condemned when he asked,
questions.A: 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you go to inquire of Baal-zebub?'
questions.B: 'How long will you go limping between two opinions?'
questions.C: 'Have you found me, O my enemy?'
questions.D: 'Why have you troubled Israel with your father's sins?'
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:21: Elijah demanded that the people stop wavering between the LORD and Baal and choose one.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Elijah's prayer on Carmel asked that the people would know 'that thou, O LORD, art God, and that thou hast turned their hearts back'. The main purpose of the contest was to
questions.A: punish Ahab for the murder of Naboth
questions.B: prove that Elijah was greater than Moses
questions.C: bring the people back to the worship of the true God
questions.D: end the drought so that trade could resume
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:36-37: the miracle was meant to turn Israel's heart back to the LORD, not to display Elijah's power.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Ahab 'did more to provoke the LORD to anger than all the kings of Israel who were before him' because he
questions.A: made peace with Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah
questions.B: refused to pay tribute to the king of Assyria
questions.C: moved the capital of Israel from Tirzah to Samaria
questions.D: married Jezebel and built a temple and altar for Baal in Samaria
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 16:31-33: Ahab married Jezebel of Sidon, served Baal, built him a house in Samaria and made an Asherah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Nebuchadnezzar said, 'Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego... there is no other god who is able to deliver in this way.' This shows that
questions.A: Nebuchadnezzar became a Jew and abolished idol worship in Babylon
questions.B: even a pagan king was forced to acknowledge the supremacy of God
questions.C: the Babylonian gods were regarded as equal to the God of Israel
questions.D: the fiery furnace was a test the king had planned with Daniel
questions.explanation: Daniel 3:28-29: the deliverance from the furnace made the most powerful king of the age confess the supremacy of the God of Israel.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Hezekiah broke in pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made because
questions.A: the Assyrians demanded all bronze objects as tribute
questions.B: the serpent had been made by the Canaanites and not by Moses
questions.C: the people had been burning incense to it, turning a symbol into an idol
questions.D: it had rusted and could no longer be used for healing
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:4: the people called it Nehushtan and worshipped it; Hezekiah destroyed even a sacred relic that had become an idol.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Church members treat their late founder's chair as sacred and pray before it. They are repeating the error Hezekiah corrected when he
questions.A: built the tunnel that brought water into Jerusalem
questions.B: opened the doors of the temple that his father had shut
questions.C: stopped paying tribute to the king of Assyria
questions.D: broke the bronze serpent to which the people burned incense
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:4: an object connected with a past act of God had become an object of worship, which is idolatry.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the book of the law found in the temple was read to Josiah, he tore his clothes because
questions.A: the book showed that he was not the rightful king of Judah
questions.B: he realised how far the nation had departed from the law and feared its curses
questions.C: Hilkiah the priest had hidden the book from him for many years
questions.D: the book commanded him to pull down the temple
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:11-13: 'great is the wrath of the LORD that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not obeyed the words of this book'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Huldah the prophetess told Josiah's messengers that
questions.A: Josiah would reign for forty more years in peace if he rebuilt the altar at Bethel
questions.B: the book of the law was a forgery written by the priests and should be burned at once
questions.C: judgment would fall on Judah, but not in Josiah's days, because he had humbled himself
questions.D: the Assyrians would capture Jerusalem within one year unless the king paid tribute
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:15-20: judgment on Judah was certain, but Josiah would be gathered to his grave in peace because his heart was penitent.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Josiah defiled Topheth in the valley of the son of Hinnom so that
questions.A: the Passover lambs could be slaughtered there
questions.B: the Levites would have a place to bury the dead
questions.C: the water supply of Jerusalem would be protected
questions.D: no one might burn his son or daughter as an offering to Molech
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23:10: Josiah ended the practice of child sacrifice to Molech as part of his purge of idolatry.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Josiah kept a Passover 'such as had not been kept since the days of the judges'. This shows that true religious reform involves
questions.A: abolishing all festivals inherited from earlier generations
questions.B: restoring proper worship as well as removing what is evil
questions.C: changing the place of worship from Jerusalem to Bethel
questions.D: replacing the priests with the king's own officials
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23:21-23: after purging idolatry, Josiah renewed covenant worship according to the book of the covenant.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Hezekiah's reforms were remarkable because his father Ahaz had
questions.A: been a faithful king who kept the Passover every year
questions.B: already removed all the high places in Judah
questions.C: shut the doors of the temple and sacrificed to the gods of Damascus
questions.D: destroyed the altar of Baal on Mount Carmel
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 28:22-25 and 29:3: Ahaz closed the temple and set up altars everywhere; Hezekiah reopened and cleansed it in his first month.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At Bethel Josiah broke down the altar that Jeroboam had built and burnt bones on it, thereby fulfilling
questions.A: the words of Isaiah to Hezekiah about the Babylonians
questions.B: the promise God made to Solomon at Gibeon
questions.C: the curse Joshua pronounced on whoever rebuilt Jericho
questions.D: the prophecy of the man of God from Judah in Jeroboam's time
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23:15-18 and 1 Kings 13:1-3: the man of God had foretold that a son of David named Josiah would defile that altar.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A school rediscovers its forgotten rule book and publicly recommits every student to it. This resembles
questions.A: Hezekiah's destruction of the bronze serpent
questions.B: Josiah's covenant renewal after the book of the law was found
questions.C: Rehoboam's consultation with the young men at Shechem
questions.D: Solomon's dedication of the temple in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23:1-3: Josiah read the book to all the people and led them in a public renewal of the covenant.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When King Artaxerxes asked Nehemiah, 'For what do you make request?' Nehemiah first
questions.A: denied that anything at all was troubling him
questions.B: asked the queen to plead his case before the king
questions.C: prayed to the God of heaven before answering the king
questions.D: asked to be released from the king's service for ever
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 2:4: a quick, silent prayer in a critical moment shows Nehemiah's habit of depending on God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Nehemiah inspected the broken walls of Jerusalem by night with a few men and told no one what God had put in his heart, because he wanted to
questions.A: keep the wall unrepaired so that the king would recall him
questions.B: avoid paying the toll charged for entering the city by day
questions.C: take building materials from the houses of the nobles
questions.D: assess the task fully before announcing his plan and alerting opponents
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 2:11-16: careful planning and discretion preceded his public appeal, 'Come, let us build the wall of Jerusalem'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Sanballat and Tobiah plotted to attack the builders, Nehemiah said, 'We prayed to our God and set a guard as a protection against them day and night.' This teaches that
questions.A: prayer makes any human precaution unnecessary
questions.B: prayer and practical vigilance go together
questions.C: guards are more reliable than prayer in a crisis
questions.D: believers should abandon their work when threatened
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 4:9 and 4:17: the people prayed and also built with a weapon in one hand, combining faith with action.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A co-operative leader stops wealthy members from charging crippling interest to poorer members in a time of hardship. He is acting as Nehemiah did when he
questions.A: threw Tobiah's furniture out of the temple chamber
questions.B: shut the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath began
questions.C: confronted the nobles who were exacting interest and taking children as slaves
questions.D: refused Sanballat's invitation to meet in the plain of Ono
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:1-13: Nehemiah rebuked the nobles and made them restore fields, houses and interest to their brothers.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Nehemiah did not take the food allowance due to him as governor for twelve years because
questions.A: he wanted the people to pay him a larger sum after the wall was built
questions.B: the king of Persia had forbidden governors to receive allowances
questions.C: he was wealthy enough to build a palace from his own funds
questions.D: the burden on the people was already heavy and he feared God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:14-18: 'because of the fear of God' he did not lord it over the people as former governors had done.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Nehemiah ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be shut before the Sabbath and set his servants over them in order to
questions.A: prevent the Samaritans from worshipping in the temple
questions.B: stop traders from selling goods in the city on the Sabbath
questions.C: protect the city from an attack by the Ammonites
questions.D: collect a tax from every merchant who entered the city
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:15-22: he warned the merchants who camped outside that he would lay hands on them if they came again.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Sanballat mocked, 'If a fox goes up on it he will break down their stone wall!' Yet the wall soon reached half its height because
questions.A: Sanballat later changed his mind and helped
questions.B: the king of Persia sent soldiers to build it
questions.C: the people had a mind to work
questions.D: Nehemiah hired builders from Egypt
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 4:6: 'So we built the wall... for the people had a mind to work'; unity and commitment overcame ridicule.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the wall was finished in fifty-two days, the surrounding nations were afraid because
questions.A: the Jews had recovered the ark of the covenant
questions.B: the Persian army had arrived to garrison Jerusalem
questions.C: Nehemiah threatened to invade Samaria next
questions.D: they perceived that the work had been accomplished with the help of God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:15-16: the enemies 'fell greatly in their own esteem; for they perceived that this work had been accomplished with the help of our God'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Nehemiah's decision to leave his comfortable post as cup-bearer in Susa to rebuild Jerusalem shows
questions.A: ambition to become king of Judah in place of the Persian governors
questions.B: patriotic concern for God's people that put their welfare above personal comfort
questions.C: fear that Artaxerxes was about to dismiss him from the palace
questions.D: a desire to escape a famine that had struck the land of Persia
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 1-2: his weeping, fasting and request to go show a selfless concern for the 'great trouble and shame' of his people.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego told the king, 'Our God whom we serve is able to deliver us... But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods.' The words 'but if not' show that
questions.A: they expected the king to change his mind at the last moment
questions.B: they doubted that God had the power to save them
questions.C: their obedience did not depend on being rescued
questions.D: they were prepared to bow if the fire proved too hot
questions.explanation: Daniel 3:17-18: their faith was in God Himself, not in a guaranteed outcome; they would obey whether delivered or not.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After the three Hebrews came out of the furnace unharmed, Nebuchadnezzar
questions.A: sent them back to Jerusalem with the temple vessels
questions.B: threw Daniel into the furnace in their place
questions.C: ordered that the golden image be made even larger
questions.D: decreed that no people should speak against their God and promoted them
questions.explanation: Daniel 3:28-30: the king blessed their God, made a decree protecting their faith and promoted them in Babylon.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Daniel's enemies said, 'We shall not find any ground for complaint against this Daniel unless we find it in connection with the law of his God.' This shows that
questions.A: Daniel had broken several Persian laws in secret
questions.B: his conduct was so blameless that only his faith could be used against him
questions.C: the law of God permitted Daniel to disobey the king
questions.D: Darius had already decided to remove Daniel from office
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:4-5: Daniel was faithful and without error, so his rivals attacked the one thing he would never compromise.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A Christian student keeps praying openly in the hostel despite a ban on religious activities, just as Daniel prayed with his windows open after the decree was signed. The student is showing
questions.A: the three Hebrews' refusal to eat the food from the king's table
questions.B: Esther's silence about her nationality in the palace of Susa
questions.C: Daniel's courage in maintaining his devotion to God under threat
questions.D: Nehemiah's caution in inspecting the walls of Jerusalem by night
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:10: Daniel neither hid nor changed his practice of prayer when it became dangerous.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: King Darius was greatly distressed and laboured till sundown to rescue Daniel but could not, because
questions.A: the satraps had locked the king in his own palace
questions.B: the lions had already been released into the city
questions.C: Daniel refused to accept a pardon from a pagan king
questions.D: a law of the Medes and Persians once signed could not be changed
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:14-15: the king's rash decree trapped him; only God could deliver Daniel, and He shut the lions' mouths.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Before going to the king uninvited, Esther asked Mordecai to gather all the Jews in Susa to fast for three days, saying, 'If I perish, I perish.' This shows
questions.A: reckless disregard for the law of the Persian court
questions.B: courage combined with dependence on God through fasting
questions.C: confidence that the king could never refuse her anything
questions.D: a plan to escape from Susa if the king was angry
questions.explanation: Esther 4:15-16: Esther prepared for a life-risking act by seeking God's help together with her people.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Mordecai told Esther, 'Who knows whether you have not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?' He meant that
questions.A: she should flee the palace before Haman's decree took effect
questions.B: the king would soon divorce her as he had divorced Vashti
questions.C: God may have placed her in the palace so that she could save her people
questions.D: her position as queen was purely a matter of good luck
questions.explanation: Esther 4:14: Mordecai saw God's providence in Esther's position and called her to use it courageously.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A nurse refuses to falsify a report even after being threatened with dismissal, saying, 'God can protect me, but even if He does not, I will not lie.' Her attitude echoes that of
questions.A: the three Hebrews before Nebuchadnezzar
questions.B: Jonah before the sailors in the storm
questions.C: Gehazi before Naaman the Syrian
questions.D: Saul before Samuel at Gilgal
questions.explanation: Daniel 3:17-18: like Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, she obeys God regardless of whether deliverance follows.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The lesson common to Daniel in the lions' den and the three Hebrews in the furnace is that
questions.A: God protects those who remain faithful to Him under persecution
questions.B: believers should avoid serving in pagan governments
questions.C: God always removes His people from danger before it comes
questions.D: kings have no authority at all over the people of God
questions.explanation: Daniel 3 and 6: faithfulness under threat was met by divine protection, and God was glorified before pagan kings.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jonah went down to Joppa and boarded a ship for Tarshish in order to
questions.A: flee from the presence of the LORD and avoid preaching to Nineveh
questions.B: reach Nineveh more quickly by travelling over the sea
questions.C: trade with the Phoenicians before starting his mission
questions.D: escape a famine that had struck the land of Israel
questions.explanation: Jonah 1:3: Tarshish lay in the opposite direction from Nineveh; Jonah was running from his commission.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: During the storm the sailors rowed hard to bring the ship to land, prayed to the LORD not to hold them guilty, and only then threw Jonah into the sea. Their behaviour shows that
questions.A: the pagan sailors showed more reverence and compassion than the runaway prophet
questions.B: sailors in those days were secretly worshippers of the God of Israel
questions.C: Jonah had persuaded them to become Jews during the voyage
questions.D: they had intended to kill Jonah from the moment he boarded
questions.explanation: Jonah 1:13-16: the sailors' reluctance and their fear of the LORD contrast with Jonah's disobedience and indifference.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jonah preached, 'Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!' the king of Nineveh
questions.A: rose from his throne, put on sackcloth, sat in ashes and decreed a fast for man and beast
questions.B: had Jonah arrested as a foreign spy and thrown into prison until the forty days had passed
questions.C: sent his army to attack the land of Israel in revenge for the insult to his great city
questions.D: ignored the message completely and held a feast on the fortieth day to mock the prophet
questions.explanation: Jonah 3:6-9: the king humbled himself and commanded everyone to turn from evil and violence, hoping God would relent.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The king of Nineveh commanded, 'Let every one turn from his evil way and from the violence which is in his hands.' This shows that genuine repentance involves
questions.A: a concrete change of conduct and not merely outward signs of sorrow
questions.B: fasting and sackcloth only, without any change of behaviour
questions.C: offering sacrifices in the temple at Jerusalem
questions.D: paying compensation to the prophet who brought the message
questions.explanation: Jonah 3:8-10: God saw 'how they turned from their evil way' and repented of the evil He had said He would do.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God used the plant that sheltered Jonah and then withered to teach him that
questions.A: God's compassion for Nineveh's people was far greater than Jonah's concern for a plant
questions.B: prophets should never rest in the shade while waiting for judgment to fall
questions.C: the east wind was a sign of the coming destruction of Nineveh
questions.D: Jonah should have planted a tree instead of building a booth
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:10-11: 'You pity the plant... and should not I pity Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than 120,000 persons?'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A church youth refuses to join an outreach to a neighbourhood notorious for crime, saying, 'They deserve whatever comes to them.' His attitude resembles
questions.A: Jonah's attitude towards the people of Nineveh
questions.B: the sailors' attitude towards Jonah in the storm
questions.C: the king of Nineveh's attitude towards God's warning
questions.D: Nehemiah's attitude towards the nobles of Judah
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:1-2: Jonah was angry that God spared Nineveh; he wanted judgment on Israel's enemies rather than their salvation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God's decision to spare Nineveh after Jonah had announced its destruction shows that
questions.A: God's threats of judgment are conditional on the response of the people
questions.B: Jonah's prophecy was false and he was not a true prophet
questions.C: God changes His mind without any reason at all
questions.D: Nineveh was never really in danger of destruction
questions.explanation: Jonah 3:10 (compare Jeremiah 18:7-8): when a nation turns from evil, God relents of the disaster He announced.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In his anger Jonah said, 'I knew that thou art a gracious God and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love.' This reveals that Jonah
questions.A: fled because he did not want God's mercy extended to Israel's enemies
questions.B: did not believe that God was merciful before the events at Nineveh
questions.C: had never heard of God's character until the plant withered
questions.D: expected God to destroy Israel instead of Nineveh
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:2: Jonah's complaint shows he had fled precisely because he expected God to forgive the repentant Ninevites.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The book of Jonah teaches Israel that
questions.A: God's love and salvation extend to all nations, not to Israel alone
questions.B: prophets may refuse missions they consider too dangerous
questions.C: God never sends His messengers to Gentile cities
questions.D: only the people of Israel are able to repent
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:11: the book ends with God's compassion for a Gentile city, correcting a narrow view of God's love.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: Amos declared in God's name, 'I hate, I despise your feasts... But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.' This teaches that
questions.A: worship is unacceptable to God when it is not accompanied by justice
questions.B: God abolished all feasts and sacrifices in the time of Amos
questions.C: justice is a substitute for worship, so that worship is unnecessary
questions.D: feasts should be held near rivers and flowing streams
questions.explanation: Amos 5:21-24: elaborate worship cannot cover up the oppression of the poor; God requires justice first.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: A trader uses a measuring cup with a false bottom so that customers receive less than they pay for. Amos condemned this practice when he spoke against those who
questions.A: make the ephah small and the shekel great and deal deceitfully with false balances
questions.B: lie upon beds of ivory and sing idle songs to the sound of the harp
questions.C: trample the head of the poor into the dust of the earth
questions.D: go to Bethel and transgress, and to Gilgal and multiply transgression
questions.explanation: Amos 8:4-6: dishonest weights and measures that cheat the needy are singled out as sins God will never forget.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: When Amaziah, priest of Bethel, told Amos to go and prophesy in Judah, Amos replied that he was no prophet nor a prophet's son but a herdsman whom the LORD had taken from following the flock. His reply showed that
questions.A: his authority came from God's direct call and not from a professional prophetic guild
questions.B: he was too poor to travel back to Judah as Amaziah had demanded
questions.C: he had agreed to stop prophesying in the king's sanctuary
questions.D: he intended to become a priest at Bethel himself
questions.explanation: Amos 7:14-15: Amos rejected the suggestion that he prophesied for a living; he spoke because the LORD had sent him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: Hosea said in God's name, 'I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.' A church that raises huge offerings while its members cheat and hate one another is failing in what Hosea called
questions.A: steadfast love and the knowledge of God
questions.B: burnt offerings and sacrifice
questions.C: the payment of tithes and first fruits
questions.D: the observance of new moons and Sabbaths
questions.explanation: Hosea 6:6: God values covenant love and true knowledge of Him above ritual; Jesus quoted this verse twice.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: Hosea blamed the priests for the moral decay of Israel because they
questions.A: had rejected the knowledge of God and fed on the sins of the people
questions.B: had moved the sanctuary from Bethel to Jerusalem
questions.C: refused to accept sacrifices from the poor
questions.D: had joined Amos in condemning the king
questions.explanation: Hosea 4:6-8: 'because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from being a priest to me... they feed on the sin of my people'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: God told Hosea to buy back his unfaithful wife for fifteen shekels of silver and a measure of barley. This act symbolised
questions.A: God's redeeming love for unfaithful Israel
