questions.B: the price of a slave in the markets of Samaria
questions.C: Hosea's poverty as a prophet without support
questions.D: the payment Israel owed to Assyria as tribute
questions.explanation: Hosea 3:1-3: 'Go again, love a woman who is beloved of a paramour... even as the LORD loves the people of Israel'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: The name Lo-ammi given to Hosea's third child meant
questions.A: 'not my people', signifying God's rejection of unfaithful Israel
questions.B: 'God sows', signifying a coming harvest of blessing
questions.C: 'not pitied', signifying that God would no longer have mercy
questions.D: 'God saves', signifying the coming deliverance from Assyria
questions.explanation: Hosea 1:9: 'Call his name Not my people, for you are not my people and I am not your God'; Lo-ruhamah meant 'not pitied'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: A landlord evicts a widow in the rainy season over a small debt and then goes to lead worship on Sunday. This illustrates what Amos condemned:
questions.A: oppression of the poor combined with outward religious observance
questions.B: the failure to pay tithes on income earned from property
questions.C: the worship of Baal alongside the LORD at Bethel
questions.D: the refusal to attend the appointed feasts in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Amos 2:6-8: those who trampled the poor also lay down beside every altar on garments taken in pledge.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: Hosea's final message, 'Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God... I will heal their faithlessness; I will love them freely,' shows that
questions.A: God's love offers restoration to those who repent even after serious unfaithfulness
questions.B: Israel had never really been unfaithful to God in the first place
questions.C: God's love is given only to those who have kept the covenant perfectly
questions.D: the northern kingdom would not be punished at all
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:1-4: the book that exposes Israel's adultery ends with an invitation to return and a promise of free, healing love.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the temple vision Isaiah cried, 'Woe is me! For I am lost,' because
questions.A: the vision of God's holiness made him conscious of his own sinfulness and his people's
questions.B: the seraphim had threatened to burn him with the live coal
questions.C: King Uzziah had just died and he feared for the nation
questions.D: he had entered the Holy of Holies without permission
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:1-5: seeing the thrice-holy LORD, Isaiah confessed that he was a man of unclean lips among a people of unclean lips.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After his lips were cleansed, Isaiah heard, 'Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?' and answered, 'Here am I! Send me.' This teaches that
questions.A: cleansing from sin leads to willing service for God
questions.B: God sends only those who volunteer before being cleansed
questions.C: prophets were chosen by casting lots in the temple
questions.D: Isaiah was appointed high priest in place of Uzziah
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:6-8: forgiveness came first, then the readiness to be sent; call follows cleansing.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Isaiah's commission included the warning that
questions.A: the people would hear but not understand, and judgment would leave only a stump
questions.B: the Assyrians would be converted by his preaching within a year
questions.C: he would be stoned by the people of Jerusalem
questions.D: no king of Judah would ever listen to him
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:9-13: the message would harden hearts until the land lay desolate, yet 'the holy seed is its stump' promised a remnant.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jeremiah objected, 'I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth,' God
questions.A: touched his mouth, put His words in it and promised to deliver him
questions.B: chose Baruch the scribe to prophesy instead of him
questions.C: gave him seven years to train under the priests at Anathoth
questions.D: struck him dumb until he agreed to go
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 1:6-9: 'Do not say, I am only a youth... Be not afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Ezekiel was told to eat the scroll written with words of lamentation, mourning and woe before speaking to Israel, in order to
questions.A: take God's message fully into himself before delivering it
questions.B: prove that he could survive without ordinary food
questions.C: destroy the evidence of God's judgment on the people
questions.D: show the exiles that the scroll tasted sweet
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:8-3:3: the prophet must first absorb the word of God; it tasted as sweet as honey though its content was judgment.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A pastor never preaches against the corruption of his wealthy members for fear of losing them. He is failing in the duty God gave Ezekiel when He appointed him
questions.A: a watchman who must warn the wicked or answer for their blood
questions.B: a priest who must offer sacrifices for the sins of the people
questions.C: a king who must judge between the rich and the poor
questions.D: a scribe who must record the history of the exile
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:17-19: if the watchman does not warn the wicked, 'his blood I will require at your hand'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A feature common to the calls of Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel is that
questions.A: God took the initiative and equipped the prophet for a difficult task
questions.B: each prophet volunteered at a festival in the temple
questions.C: each was called while serving as a priest in Babylon
questions.D: each was promised that the people would gladly accept his message
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6, Jeremiah 1 and Ezekiel 2-3: in every case God called, cleansed or strengthened the prophet and warned of resistance.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The seraphim covered their faces and their feet in the presence of the LORD. This shows
questions.A: reverence before God's overwhelming holiness
questions.B: that the seraphim were ashamed of their appearance
questions.C: that the temple was too bright for them to see
questions.D: that they were about to fly away from the throne
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:2: even sinless heavenly beings veil themselves before the thrice-holy God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God told Ezekiel, 'I have made your face hard against their faces, and your forehead hard against their foreheads,' because
questions.A: the house of Israel was rebellious, impudent and stubborn
questions.B: Ezekiel was a timid man who feared the exiles
questions.C: the Babylonians would try to torture him
questions.D: the prophet had asked God for physical strength
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:3-7 and 3:8-9: God equipped Ezekiel with resolve equal to the stubbornness of the people he was sent to.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Ezekiel rejected the proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge' in order to teach that
questions.A: each person is responsible for his own sin and will be judged individually
questions.B: children must bear the punishment for the sins of their parents
questions.C: sour grapes were forbidden food for the exiles in Babylon
questions.D: the exile was entirely the fault of the previous generation
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:2-4: 'The soul that sins shall die'; the son shall not suffer for the iniquity of the father.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A boy says, 'I keep failing because my grandfather was cursed.' Ezekiel's teaching contradicts him by insisting that
questions.A: a person is judged for his own conduct, not for his ancestors' sins
questions.B: curses pass from generation to generation without any limit
questions.C: only a priest can remove a curse from a family
questions.D: failure in examinations is always a sign of divine punishment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:20: 'The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon himself.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God said through Ezekiel, 'Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked... and not rather that he should turn from his way and live?' This shows that
questions.A: God desires the repentance of sinners rather than their punishment
questions.B: God takes no notice of the sins of the wicked
questions.C: the wicked can never escape the death they deserve
questions.D: repentance is possible only for the righteous
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:21-23: the wicked man who turns from his sins 'shall surely live; he shall not die'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A deacon says, 'I have served this church for thirty years, so my present fraud does not matter.' Ezekiel would reply that
questions.A: the righteous deeds of a man who turns to sin will not be remembered
questions.B: long service cancels out any later wrongdoing
questions.C: fraud is a minor sin compared with idolatry
questions.D: God judges only the first half of a person's life
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:24: when a righteous man turns away and does wrong, 'none of the righteous deeds which he has done shall be remembered'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In Ezekiel's vision of the valley of dry bones, God said, 'These bones are the whole house of Israel. Behold, they say, Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost.' The vision was therefore a message of
questions.A: hope that God would restore the nation the exiles thought was dead
questions.B: judgment on the exiles for failing to bury their dead
questions.C: warning that the exile would last another seventy years
questions.D: instruction on how the exiles should honour their ancestors
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:11-14: God promised to open their graves, put His Spirit in them and bring them back to their own land.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Ezekiel joined two sticks into one, marked 'Judah' and 'Joseph', to symbolise
questions.A: the reunion of Israel and Judah under one king
questions.B: the alliance between Judah and Egypt against Babylon
questions.C: the two tablets of the law kept in the ark
questions.D: the union of priests and prophets in the temple
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:15-22: 'I will make them one nation in the land... and one king shall be king over them all'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jeremiah bought a field at Anathoth from his cousin Hanamel while Jerusalem was under siege by the Babylonians. This purchase was a sign that
questions.A: God would restore His people to the land after the exile
questions.B: Jeremiah intended to flee to Anathoth before the city fell
questions.C: land prices had collapsed and the prophet was making a profit
questions.D: the Babylonians would never capture the city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:15: 'Houses and fields and vineyards shall again be bought in this land'; judgment would be followed by restoration.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God said through Jeremiah, 'Return, faithless Israel... I will not look on you in anger, for I am merciful... Only acknowledge your guilt.' The condition for restoration was
questions.A: honest acknowledgement of sin and a return to God
questions.B: payment of double tribute to the king of Babylon
questions.C: the rebuilding of the high places destroyed by Josiah
questions.D: the return of the ark from the land of the Philistines
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:12-13: mercy was offered freely, but it required repentance and confession of guilt.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A prisoner is told, 'God does not hold your past against you if you turn to Him now.' This counsel reflects the teaching of
questions.A: Ezekiel 18, that the wicked who turn from their sins shall live
questions.B: Amos 5, that God despises the feasts of Israel
questions.C: Jonah 1, that no one can flee from the presence of God
questions.D: 1 Samuel 15, that rebellion is as the sin of divination
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:21-22: 'None of the transgressions which he has committed shall be remembered against him'.
